runs.q: Compare BNPL and mada fees. Which costs us more?
runs.text:
Comparing BNPL and mada fees:

- BNPL has bank fees of SAR 77,777.36 with a fee rate of 467.9 bps.
- Mada has bank fees of SAR 135,224.42 with a fee rate of 99.5 bps.

Although BNPL has a higher fee rate, mada costs more in total bank fees (SAR 135,224.42) compared to BNPL (SAR 77,777.36). So, mada costs us more in absolute fees.

runs.q: How many invoices did ZATCA reject, and what happened to them?
runs.text: ZATCA rejected 1 invoice, classified as a "CONFIRMED_REJECTION." This rejected invoice remains in the hash chain and must be fixed by issuing a new correcting document with a new ICV; it cannot be fixed by resending the same document.

runs.q: What does not assessed mean, and how many merchant-days are not assessed?
runs.text:
"Not assessed" means a merchant-day for which the bank file has not yet arrived. The money for these days is considered in transit, not missing, and the day is neither balanced nor unbalanced until the file arrives.

Currently, there are 112 merchant-days not assessed because their bank files are pending. The expected net amount for these not assessed merchant-days is SAR 1,125,209.07.

There was also 1 correction issued and 1 transport failure retried with identical bytes, but these are separate events from the rejection.

runs.q: What is MIZAN and what does it do?
runs.text: MIZAN is an engineering reference platform for Saudi commerce businesses, using synthetic data. It demonstrates how a business can track every sale end to end, including the order, ZATCA e-invoice, card or mada payment, next-day bank settlement, and ERP general ledger. It ensures that bank and ledger records agree exactly, while complying with PDPL privacy rules and NDMO data classification. The platform runs on Microsoft Fabric with Airflow, dbt, and OpenLineage.

ZATCA (Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority) is the authority that runs Saudi Arabia's e-invoicing system called FATOORA. In Phase 2, business-to-business (standard) invoices must be cleared by ZATCA before they are valid (CLEARANCE), while business-to-consumer (simplified) invoices are reported within 24 hours (REPORTING). Each invoice is digitally signed and linked to the previous one in a chain.

زاتكا (ZATCA) هي هيئة الزكاة والضرائب والجمارك في السعودية، وهي المسؤولة عن تشغيل نظام الفوترة الإلكترونية في المملكة المعروف باسم "فاتورة". في المرحلة الثانية من النظام، يجب أن تتم الموافقة على فواتير الأعمال إلى الأعمال (الفواتير القياسية) من قبل زاتكا لتصبح صالحة (مرحلة الموافقة)، بينما يتم الإبلاغ عن فواتير الأعمال إلى المستهلك (الفواتير المبسطة) خلال 24 ساعة. كل فاتورة يتم توقيعها وربطها بالفاتورة السابقة في سلسلة.

disputes.note: A dispute ratio on small volumes is noise, so the card-scheme programmes judge a ratio AND a minimum dispute count. The ratio alone would flag most of the portfolio; both together flag one merchant. Thresholds are read from secondary sources, not the scheme rulebooks, and the window is this dataset's span, not a calendar month.

known_platform_behaviour.lakehouse_sql_endpoint_lag: After the ZATCA step rewrote slv.zatca_invoice_documents, the first dbt build still failed on the pre-rewrite snapshot: the Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint syncs asynchronously behind the Delta tables. The identical build a minute later passed 91/91. Worth knowing before trusting a dbt result taken immediately after a Spark write.

brz.zatca_invoices_raw.note: Two versions of every request: the original and the price-corrected re-send. Bronze is append-only by design; Silver takes the latest.

fabric.note: Re-run of the 2026-11-14 deployment after six item prices were corrected locally. Bronze is append-only, so every source file re-landed as corrections rather than duplicates: the landed_rows below are the rows whose payload actually changed, not the file sizes. This run also exposed a real defect -- see zatca_chain.defect_found.

zatca_chain.defect_found: The first run of this step on corrected data doubled slv.zatca_invoice_documents to 50,002 rows: zatca_land joined ctl.invoice_outbox to brz.zatca_invoices_raw on request_id, and Bronze held two versions of every request, so each outbox row fanned into two. dbt's source_unique test caught it (25,001 duplicate invoice_uuid) and refused to publish Gold. Fixed by reading Bronze through _latest(), as every other Bronze reader already did; pinned by test_a_corrected_zatca_resend_does_not_double_the_silver_documents, which was verified to fail without the fix. The seconds and counts above are the re-run with the fix applied.

zatca_chain_predates_the_price_correctio.gap_it_exposes: The correction moved Silver, Gold and the bank reconciliation, and left the tax ledger on the old amount with no credit note raised. See HONESTY.md row 29.
zatca_chain_predates_the_price_correctio.test: apps/command-center/src/command-center/shape.spec.ts compares the chain's full shape exactly and bounds only the money; the exact comparison resumes when the totals meet again.
zatca_chain_predates_the_price_correctio.why: run_zatca skips every request_id already in ctl.invoice_outbox, so a signed invoice is never re-priced. The chain on Fabric still carries the prices it was signed with on 2026-11-14, and the Fabric figure is exactly the local total from before the 2026-11-16 BR-KSA-50 price correction. Making the two agree would mean re-signing a cleared tax document, which a ZATCA chain must not do.

known_validator_defects.BR-KSA-50: The rule compares line VAT in IEEE doubles with no tolerance: for a 96.00 line it computes 14.399999999999999 and rejects our exact 14.40. MIZAN's money is Decimal.
known_validator_defects.R: The QR stage expects tags 8 and 9 to carry the signature's R and S; ZATCA's published spec defines them as the public key and the certificate signature. We follow the spec.
known_validator_defects.S: See R: same mismatch between the SDK build and the published QR specification.
known_validator_defects.vatTotal: BR-KSA-68 forces a tax currency code, BR-KSA-EN16931-09 then forces a second TaxTotal, and the QR check sums both before comparing. No invoice can satisfy all three unless the QR states double the real VAT.

zatca_sdk.licence: LGPL v3 (bundled in the SDK; never redistributed by this repo)
zatca_sdk.note: XSD, EN 16931 and the KSA business rules pass. The QR stage cannot pass: two KSA rules force a second TaxTotal that the QR check then sums, and this SDK build reads QR tags 8 and 9 as the signature's R and S rather than the key and certificate signature that ZATCA's published specification defines. See HONESTY.md.
